## M0. Mathematical carriers and what is merely syntax

A finite matrix of size r by c is an entry function on {0,...,r−1}×{0,...,c−1}. Multiplication is the finite ordered sum
\[
(AB)_{ij}=\sum_{k=0}^{m-1}A_{ik}B_{kj}.
\]
The implementation's coefficient carrier is a free expression syntax consisting of rational constants, named symbols, addition, multiplication, and negation. An environment assigns an arbitrary rational value to each symbol. Evaluation recursively interprets the expression. Syntactic equality is stronger than equality after evaluation; finite products retain zero summands in their syntax.
source_paragraphs.counts_as_scientific_closure: Only the expressly stated local scope.

source_paragraphs.exact_text: In particular, naming symbols for an inverse, a sine, a cosine, or a normalized coefficient imposes no algebraic or analytic relation. An arbitrary environment need not make an inverse symbol the reciprocal of a normalizer. There is no automatic real or complex Hilbert-space semantics, absolute square, square root, arccos, norm, or unitarity predicate on this syntax.
source_paragraphs.counts_as_scientific_closure: Only the expressly stated local scope.

source_paragraphs.exact_text: For a circuit list in temporal order g₁,...,gₖ, the matrix fold is gₖ⋯g₁. Alignment of gate labels with a supplied matrix list certifies label agreement, not the supplied matrices' physical meaning. A gate's “proved” field is a Boolean data field, not a proof term of unitarity.

source_paragraphs.exact_text: The common path-isolation mechanism is finite-sum elimination: if every summand vanishes, the sum vanishes; if only k₀ survives, the sum is its k₀ term; if only distinct k₀,k₁ survive, it is their sum. One proves these by induction on a duplicate-free finite enumeration, splitting whether the head is a surviving index. Matrix-entry versions follow by evaluating the symbolic multiplication fold. These are ordinary finite arithmetic providers, not quantum oracle constructions.

source_paragraphs.exact_text: ## M3. The seven global sparse slots

For the concrete fourth-order family, the active global slot offsets are
\[
(o_0,\ldots,o_6)=(N-2,N-1,0,1,2,N-3,3)
\]
and the total function assigns zero offset to other slots. Define
\[
F_s(i)=(o_s+i)\bmod N.
\]
This is the actual retained global-slot address formula, including zero-amplitude slots. It is not a row-dependent list of nonzero columns.
source_paragraphs.counts_as_scientific_closure: Only the expressly stated local scope.

source_paragraphs.exact_text:
The reverse-slot table is
\[
(\rho(0),\ldots,\rho(6))=(4,3,2,1,0,6,5),
\]
with default value 2 outside that set. On slots below 7 it is an involution and hence injective. It always lands below 8; on active slots it lands below 7. For n≥3, N≥8, and i<N,
\[
F_{\rho(s)}(F_s(i))=i
\]
holds even for encoded s=7, because both the default offset and the selected reverse slot's offset are zero. That eighth encoded value is not thereby an active κ=7 source slot.
source_paragraphs.counts_as_scientific_closure: Only the expressly stated local scope.

source_paragraphs.exact_text:
The proof is finite-table arithmetic. Opposite offsets add to N, the zero pair adds to zero, and reduction modulo N cancels a multiple of N. Composition has the shared form
\[
F_t(F_s(i))=(((o_t+o_s)\bmod N)+i)\bmod N.
\]
If 0≤a<N and i<N and (a+i) mod N=i, then a=0: split a+i<N and N≤a+i<2N. If a<2N and a mod N=0, then a is either 0 or N, by the same split. Thus for active slots s,t<7 a return to i forces their offset sum to be 0 or N. Inspection of the seven offsets, distinct for N≥8, forces t=ρ(s). Applying a reverse shift to equal addresses then proves same-row slot injectivity.
source_paragraphs.counts_as_scientific_closure: Only the expressly stated local scope.

source_paragraphs.exact_text: ## M5. Register splicing and the precise safety claim

For a compound nonnegative basis index j, set
\[
L=2^{1+n},\qquad H=2^{1+2n},\qquad
l=j\bmod L,\qquad h=\lfloor j/H\rfloor.
\]
Extract the row as floor(j/2) mod N and the old address as floor(j/L) mod N. The padded and sparse parts of the latter are its low w bits and next ℓ bits.
source_paragraphs.counts_as_scientific_closure: Only the expressly stated local scope.

source_paragraphs.exact_text:
Writing a computed address a into the address region is the literal splice
\[
I(j)=l+aL+hH.
\]
When a<N, l+aL<H since 0≤l<L and a+1≤N. It follows that I(j) mod L=l, floor(I(j)/L) mod N=a, and floor(I(j)/H)=h. Consequently the low ancilla-and-row region and every high bit above the address register are preserved. If j<2ᵀ and 1+2n≤T, then h<2^{T-(1+2n)} and the same inequality gives I(j)<2ᵀ.
source_paragraphs.counts_as_scientific_closure: Only the expressly stated local scope.

source_paragraphs.exact_text:
The bit-slice bridge is
\[
((x\gg b)\mathbin{\&}(2^q-1))=\lfloor x/2^b\rfloor\bmod2^q.
\]
It follows bit by bit from masking and shifting. This converts physical-looking slice notation into ordinary division/remainder arithmetic.

## M9. The coefficient-function clean branch and its unresolved completion

Assign each grid label i a distinct formal function symbol fᵢ. The intended normalized value is fᵢ times a named inverse symbol for N_f; no actual function evaluation, inverse law, or bound follows from the naming.
source_paragraphs.counts_as_scientific_closure: Only the expressly stated local scope.

source_paragraphs.exact_text:
The function workspace occupies m_f bits starting immediately above the indicator. For a compound index j, extract that workspace value and clear those bits to obtain z(j). Record the row value separately. On a clean-workspace input column j, the literal matrix skeleton prescribes
\[
U_{i,j}=
\begin{cases}
f_{\operatorname{row}(j)}\,\nu_f,&i=z(j),\\
0,&i\ne z(j)\text{ and the output workspace is clean},\\
q_{i,j,\operatorname{row}(j)},&\text{otherwise},
\end{cases}
\]
where \(\nu_f\) and every \(q\) are free symbols. On a nonclean input column every entry is a completion symbol. Thus the clean branch is genuinely wired into the matrix formula, and off-branch clean-workspace entries really are zero. The unresolved rows are not merely an “orthogonal remainder” vector that has already been constructed: their entries are independent placeholders. In particular, the formula does not enforce preservation of the system label in those completion rows, normalizer bounds, column normalization, orthogonality, or full-space unitarity.

source_paragraphs.exact_text: ## M10. Exact register exchange and indicator basis permutations

Let b₁(j) and b₂(j) be the two n-bit slices beginning at positions 1 and 1+n. Set d=b₁ XOR b₂ and
\[
W(j)=j\operatorname{XOR}(d\ll1)\operatorname{XOR}(d\ll(1+n)).
\]
The difference d is below 2ⁿ. At each bit in the first slice, XOR with d changes b₁ to b₂; at each bit in the second it changes b₂ to b₁. Other bits are untouched. Consequently the new difference is b₂ XOR b₁=d. Applying the same two shifted masks twice cancels, so W(W(j))=j.
source_paragraphs.counts_as_scientific_closure: Only the expressly stated local scope.

source_paragraphs.exact_text: The finite-range argument is separate: an x<2ʷ shifted by b positions is below 2ᵀ when w+b≤T, because x·2ᵇ<2ʷ·2ᵇ≤2ᵀ. Both shifted masks fit in the total basis width, and XOR of values below 2ᵀ remains below 2ᵀ. Thus W restricts to a finite basis involution. Injectivity follows by applying W again; the preimage of y is W(y), so it is surjective.
source_paragraphs.counts_as_scientific_closure: Only the expressly stated local scope.

source_paragraphs.exact_text: For the indicator, its bit position q obeys q≥1+n and q<T for every parameter record, even when the informal simplification q=1+2n is inapplicable. A value shifted above position 1+n has no effect on the n-bit row slice. Therefore the bulk predicate is unchanged by the indicator map J. Its controlled toggle mask is the same on the second application, so J(J(j))=j. The toggle is either zero or one in-range bit, establishing finite-range preservation, then finite injectivity and surjectivity by the same involution argument. The fixed n=1 and n=3 cases are finite specializations, not the basis of this arbitrary-width argument.
source_paragraphs.counts_as_scientific_closure: Only the expressly stated local scope.

source_paragraphs.exact_text: For either map F, the literal zero/one matrix is \(P_{ij}=1\) iff \(i=F(j)\). Each column has its unique 1 at F(j); surjectivity gives a 1 in every row and injectivity makes that 1 unique. These are exact finite permutation-matrix statements. The module does not additionally instantiate an analytic unitary predicate, nor does the placeholder swap label on wire indices (0,0) constitute a physical decomposition of the n-register swap. No Clifford+T, connectivity, or finite-bit synthesis cost is deduced.

source_paragraphs.exact_text: ## M11. General address splices and reconstruction of clean indices

For any proposed n-bit address v, extend M5's splice to
\[
S(j,v)=(j\bmod L)+vL+\lfloor j/H\rfloor H.
\]
The same no-carry argument proves preservation of the low region and high tail and exact extraction of v. It also proves
\[
S(S(j,v),u)=S(j,u)\quad(v<N).
\]
No bound on u is needed for that algebraic overwrite identity. The original index reconstructs exactly:
\[
S(j,\operatorname{address}(j))=j.
\]
This is the two-level quotient/remainder decomposition of j, not a choice of a representative or a quotient type.
source_paragraphs.counts_as_scientific_closure: Only the expressly stated local scope.

source_paragraphs.exact_text: A clean encoded sparse value for a slot s is c(s)=s·2ʷ. Its padded low w bits vanish. If ℓ≤n and s<2^ℓ, then c(s)<2ⁿ; extracting its sparse slice recovers s. Conversely, under width compatibility and padded cleanliness, the old address register value equals c(extracted sparse slot): zero remainder modulo 2ʷ removes the low term in the quotient/remainder decomposition, and the n-bit range removes an additional sparse-slice wrap.

source_paragraphs.exact_text: ## M12. Explicit post-exchange clean preimage and its precise uniqueness scope

Let a=F_s(r) for an active input with row r and slot s. After its address image and register exchange, the new row is a and the address block contains r. Define C(j) by keeping this post-exchange low region and high tail and splicing the clean encoded reverse slot c(ρ(s)) into the address block.
source_paragraphs.counts_as_scientific_closure: Only the expressly stated local scope.

source_paragraphs.exact_text:
The reverse slot is below 8 and fits the three-bit sparse register. For n≥3 it fits the n-bit address region. Splice safety keeps C(j) finite whenever j is finite. It is padded-clean by construction, and its extracted sparse slot is ρ(s). The row is still a, so its recomputed address is
\[
F_{\rho(s)}(a)=F_{\rho(s)}(F_s(r))=r.
\]
Applying the forward image to C(j) therefore replaces its address block with the post-exchange address r while preserving all other regions, yielding the post-exchange index exactly. This is the mechanism behind the candidate-check Boolean, not merely an unexplained finite check.
source_paragraphs.counts_as_scientific_closure: Only the expressly stated local scope.

source_paragraphs.exact_text: Some intermediate interfaces ask only for a clean encoded source and allow the eighth encoded slot, whereas the final active domain also requires s<7. The former range/image consequences do not establish active-domain membership or uniqueness. On the active domain, ρ(s)<7, so C(j) is itself active. Any other active clean preimage of the same post-exchange index equals C(j) by M11's active-domain image injectivity.

exact_definition_region_lines:
structure BandedSparseAccessPostSwapCleanup
    (p : OneTermRobinParameters)
    (source post pre : Fin (qubitDim (oneTermRobinTotalQubits p))) where
  postSwap :
    post.val = swapOracleImage p (bandedSparseAccessPaperImage p source.val)
  preimage : post.val = bandedSparseAccessPaperImage p pre.val
  preCleanInput : bandedSparseAccessPaperCleanInput p pre.val = true
  preAddressBound : bandedSparseAccessPaperAddress p pre.val < (1 <<< p.n)
  daggerEntry : (oneTermRobinGate_O_D_BS_dagger p).matrix pre post = Coeff.rat 1
  preRowPreserved :
    (bandedSparseAccessPaperColumnContract p pre.val).rowPreserved = true
  preAddressWritten :
    (bandedSparseAccessPaperColumnContract p pre.val).addressWritten = true
  preAddressInRange :
    (bandedSparseAccessPaperColumnContract p pre.val).addressInRange = true
  preImageNoSpill :
    (bandedSparseAccessPaperColumnContract p pre.val).imageNoSpill = true
  postRow_eq_preRow :
    (bandedSparseAccessPaperRegisters p post.val).rowValue =
      (bandedSparseAccessPaperRegisters p pre.val).rowValue
  postOd_eq_preAddress :
    (bandedSparseAccessPaperRegisters p post.val).odRegisterValue =
      bandedSparseAccessPaperAddress p pre.val

QuantumBlockEncoding.GHL2025.BandedSpars.name: QuantumBlockEncoding.GHL2025.BandedSparseAccessPostSwapCleanup
exact_definition_region_lines:
structure BandedSparseAccessPostSwapCleanup
    (p : OneTermRobinParameters)
    (source post pre : Fin (qubitDim (oneTermRobinTotalQubits p))) where
  postSwap :
    post.val = swapOracleImage p (bandedSparseAccessPaperImage p source.val)
  preimage : post.val = bandedSparseAccessPaperImage p pre.val
  preCleanInput : bandedSparseAccessPaperCleanInput p pre.val = true
  preAddressBound : bandedSparseAccessPaperAddress p pre.val < (1 <<< p.n)
  daggerEntry : (oneTermRobinGate_O_D_BS_dagger p).matrix pre post = Coeff.rat 1
  preRowPreserved :
    (bandedSparseAccessPaperColumnContract p pre.val).rowPreserved = true
  preAddressWritten :
    (bandedSparseAccessPaperColumnContract p pre.val).addressWritten = true
  preAddressInRange :
    (bandedSparseAccessPaperColumnContract p pre.val).addressInRange = true
  preImageNoSpill :
    (bandedSparseAccessPaperColumnContract p pre.val).imageNoSpill = true
  postRow_eq_preRow :
    (bandedSparseAccessPaperRegisters p post.val).rowValue =
      (bandedSparseAccessPaperRegisters p pre.val).rowValue
  postOd_eq_preAddress :
    (bandedSparseAccessPaperRegisters p post.val).odRegisterValue =
      bandedSparseAccessPaperAddress p pre.val

The WIP's lexical header endpoint for some let-bearing theorems was incomplete; this successor explicitly corrects it by locating the actual theorem proof delimiter. All 405 header endpoints lie within their actual code envelopes.

Outer carrier/data binders are classified TYPING_DATA. Outer logical assumptions are explicitly listed as LOCAL_HELPER_PREMISE, not silently marked TYPING or authenticated paper SOURCE. Each is part of the stated local arithmetic/conditional-interface theorem; none is promoted to an assumption of the unproved final one-term block-encoding claim. Quantifiers and implication antecedents inside conclusions are retained verbatim in the exact header rather than omitted from the audited statement.

Against the unavailable original paper, SOURCE/STANDING/RULED status is UNAUTHENTICATED, not falsely EXCESS-free. No approved correction is inferred. There is no scientific theorem in this target purporting to deliver the final block encoding with normalized PREPARE/oracle/cleanup premises added as source hypotheses; those advertised final claims are data records. Source hypothesis = theorem binder; proof ingredient = dependency edge is preserved for any future such Anchor.
Project-owned contract expansion:
- OneTermRobinParameters: four unrestricted Nat fields. No positivity, width or analytic promise.
- RobinRegisterPartition: six Nat widths; arithmetic totals, not a physical-cleanup proposition.
- RobinCircuitSkeleton: oracle/operation strings, bulk bounds and width data. No executable/unitary field.
- RobinGamma1/2/3 and RobinWavefunctionDecomposition: numeric ranges and symbolic prefactors plus remainder Booleans, not state-vector equations.
- ObligationRecord: description String, source String, proved Bool default false. proved=true is not a proof of the described proposition.

- RobinProofObligations: ten ObligationRecord fields (indicator, sparse amplitude, sparse access, function amplitude, boundary rotation, circuit unitarity, block extraction, resources, cleanup, ghost elimination); all default false, no hidden Prop.
- BandedSparseAccessPaperContract: register/data strings plus seven ObligationRecords (clean domain, width, address range, no spill, forward action, dagger cleanup, unitary extension). All are data.

- DerivativeOracleContract(n): stencil/bandwidth/finite Coeff matrix; sparseCorrect is data; bandwidth_eq is the actual local equality bandwidth=stencil.width. This equality is a logical field, not paper oracle correctness.
- FunctionOracleContract(n): piece count/normalizer data and amplitudeCorrect ObligationRecord, no amplitude theorem.
- OneTermRobinTheoremData: normalizer/signal/error/resource fields and the ten-obligation bundle above, not a block-encoding certificate.

- PaperColumnContract: extracted/image data and executable row/address/range/no-spill Booleans plus four copied obligations. Real safety theorems are separate local proofs.
